annotation.title_clean: Automated Verification of Social Laws for Continuous Time Multi-Robot Systems
annotation.title_en: Automated Verification of Social Laws for Continuous Time Multi-Robot Systems
annotation.venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Third AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-19)
annotation.summary_en: AAAI-19 technical paper on verifying the robustness of "social laws" (action restrictions coordinating autonomous agents) for multi-robot systems with durative, concurrent actions. It compiles verification into temporal planning and evaluates it on a real multi-robot system and PDDL domains. It is a computational coordination method, not legal or policy governance.
key_provisions_or_claims: Defines robustness of social laws in a continuous-time setting with concurrent actions.
Compiles robustness verification into a temporal planning problem, in polynomial time.
Social law is robust if every agent can reach its goal whatever the others do.
Evaluated on a real multi-robot system and PDDL 2.1 domains.
Proving unsolvability with temporal planners (OPTIC) remains a limitation.
